incidents.vector: Cyberattack beginning Nov. 19 impacted IT systems and the legislature's website; the intrusion method and whether ransomware was involved have not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: The Legislature's website and certain IT systems were taken offline as a precaution while outside cybersecurity specialists investigate. No other West Virginia state agencies were affected.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack claimed by the extortion group 'n0n,' which listed the retailer on its dark-web leak site; the group has been observed using AI coding agents to write and debug its attack scripts.
incidents.impact: Online ordering and in-store transaction systems were disrupted over the prior weekend, forcing roughly 100 U.S. stores onto alternative transaction procedures. Systems were restored by Nov. 20; no evidence yet that customer financial data was stolen.

incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking operators used the autonomous AI penetration-testing framework Cairn to discover and exploit an unpatched path-traversal zero-day in an open-source medical imaging AI application, gaining shell access to university networks.
incidents.impact: Two East Asian universities were breached. Amazon Threat Intelligence discovered the attacker's exposed Cairn server, had the underlying open-source flaw fixed, and worked with a government partner to notify the affected institutions.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in the mobile banking app platform of shared IT supplier Wellington IT, exposing payee/payment details for credit union members who used the affected apps.
incidents.impact: More than 40 Irish credit unions (and potentially U.K. members) had payment details exposed. The vulnerability was patched Oct. 6, but the breach went unreported to affected credit unions until Nov. 16 — a six-week delay regulators called 'simply not acceptable.' No evidence yet that member funds were accessed.

incidents.vector: Exploited a VMware vCenter authentication-bypass zero-day (CVE-2026-123890) via a chained intrusion that began with a separate BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day, pivoting through unmonitored internal Linux appliances to deploy custom malware and tooling (BONESAW, SAWSNAKE, SLIMSAVAGE/CAGEMATCH webshells).
incidents.impact: Attackers achieved full administrative compromise of victims' vCenter and ESXi environments — exfiltrating directory databases, forging SAML admin tokens, and bypassing MFA. Exploitation began as early as September 2026, months before public disclosure and patch availability.

incidents.victim: Equinor and Skagerak Energi (Norwegian energy companies)
incidents.vector: Breaches affecting internal IT systems disclosed on consecutive days (Nov. 17 and Nov. 18); neither company has disclosed the intrusion method, and no link between the two incidents has been confirmed.
incidents.impact: Equinor's email and internal IT systems were disrupted with no confirmed data theft or production impact; Skagerak Energi reported a similar IT-systems breach. The incidents prompted heightened alert across Norway's energy sector following an unprecedented national cyber-risk warning from NSM.

incidents.vector: Attackers used the open-source ARTEX AI hacking platform to compromise the Commission's internal HR platform, Sysper, first detected Oct. 22.
incidents.impact: The Sysper platform — used for payroll, leave requests, medical reimbursements, and translation services — was disrupted for more than 10 days. No broad staff data breach has been confirmed and no ransom demand was received; this is the Commission's third disclosed cyber incident in 2026.

incidents.victim: Mr. Cooper (Nationstar Mortgage, now part of Rocket Mortgage)
incidents.vector: Threat actors impersonated Mr. Cooper employees in phone calls to the company's IT help desk to obtain temporary passwords, bypassing multi-factor authentication to access internal information systems.
incidents.impact: Large volumes of private customer information were stolen in the November 2023 breach. NYDFS's investigation found Mr. Cooper had not completed a cybersecurity risk assessment in nearly four years. Rocket Mortgage, which acquired Mr. Cooper, will pay $6.75 million combined in penalties for this breach plus related MFA and incident-reporting failures.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed by the company.
incidents.impact: KPMG's Canadian practice is notifying clients of a security breach; the firm has not disclosed what data was affected or how the intrusion occurred.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed a test environment belonging to Rakuten's securities division.
incidents.impact: Data on more than 15 million customer accounts was stolen, including sensitive personal information for over 4.4 million accounts; passwords, PINs, and other authentication data were not among the stolen data.

incidents.vector: Brute-force attack against user accounts on Germany's e-government identity platform over the preceding weekend.
incidents.impact: At least 10,000 user accounts were compromised; officials locked the affected accounts and are notifying owners.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Hackers breached the ShebaMiles loyalty program and stole customer data; the scope of the stolen data has not been detailed.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Chargemap, an EV charging-station locator app, is notifying customers of a data breach; further details have not been released.

incidents.vector: Unconfirmed claim: the 'Gentlemen' ransomware cartel listed NVIDIA on its dark-web leak site.
incidents.impact: NVIDIA has not confirmed any security breach or data theft; the extortion claim remains unverified as of this report.

incidents.vector: A newly tracked group, dubbed 'SilentAir' by telco security firm ENEA, hacks telecom infrastructure and plants backdoors that abuse the SS7 and Diameter signaling protocols.
incidents.impact: Active since early 2025, the group has used telecom-protocol backdoors to collect device data, track subscriber locations, and intercept calls and SMS traffic of carefully selected targets across Asia; full victim scope has not been disclosed.

incidents.victim: 700+ French retail stores, food factories, and a slaughterhouse
incidents.vector: French officials, in a joint five-agency report, attributed the October hacking of commercial refrigeration systems to the Shahid Kaveh unit within the IRGC's Cyber-Electronic Command.
incidents.impact: The attack disabled refrigeration systems at more than 700 French retail locations in October, causing tens of millions of euros in losses; it follows a related August incident that disabled freezers at U.S. military commissaries.

incidents.victim: EU politicians and law enforcement officials (18 individuals)
incidents.vector: A pro-Kremlin hacktivist collective published personal information gathered on high-profile EU officials, including a foreign minister, Europol and Eurojust leadership, and journalists covering Russian influence operations.
incidents.impact: Personal details of 18 senior EU officials and three journalists were published online, raising safety and harassment concerns; no system compromise beyond the doxxing has been reported.

incidents.victim: 178+ websites including BBC, CNN, Zoom, Equifax, Ledger, HSBC, GitLab (via Optimizely)
incidents.vector: Attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into customers' project code, served from Optimizely's legitimate CDN under its own certificate.
incidents.impact: For roughly 16 hours, visitors to at least 178 top websites were served malware that swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses, skimmed payment card data at checkout, and attempted to deliver iOS/iPadOS zero-click exploit kits (Coruna, DarkSword). Optimizely patched the flaw and remediated affected accounts by Nov. 17.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached N-able's cloud platform, accessing its Mail Assure and SpamExperts servers.
incidents.impact: N-able found no evidence that customer data was stolen and is rebuilding the affected services.

incidents.vector: An attacker exploited a data analysis tool to access the AI coding platform's internal network and copy data from its databases.
incidents.impact: Stolen data includes user details and platform activity records; CodinGame has notified affected members.

incidents.vector: Attackers stole tokens across 11 different cryptocurrencies; blockchain-analysis firms and the FBI attributed the theft to the North Korean group TraderTraitor. The initial-access method has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: The theft is the largest cryptocurrency heist on record, dwarfing the $1.46 billion Bybit hack. Binance helped freeze roughly $2.8 billion of the stolen stablecoins, but about $3.25 billion in Bitcoin and Ethereum remains unrecovered.

incidents.vector: Attacker used a cloud access key Barracuda had issued to a third-party AI service provider and failed to revoke, then deployed the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework to escalate access across Barracuda's internal network and other cloud environments.
incidents.impact: The threat actor accessed Barracuda's cloud environment for nearly two days before being discovered and evicted.
